title: Digital Asset Accounting
answer: Blockchain to ledger reconciliation, token valuation, contract auditing, decentralised treasuries and impairment.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Blockchain to Ledger Reconciliation
children.blurb: Blockchain to ledger reconciliation is the practice of matching activity recorded on distributed ledgers to the entries in an organization's accounting books.

children.name: Valuing Illiquid Tokens
children.blurb: Valuing illiquid tokens covers the accounting and reporting work needed when a digital asset has no reliable, active market price.

children.name: Auditing Smart Contracts
children.blurb: Auditing smart contracts is the review of self-executing code on a blockchain to find defects, security flaws, and mismatches between what the code does and what its users or owners believe it does.

children.name: Accounting for Decentralised Treasuries
children.blurb: Accounting for decentralised treasuries covers the recognition, measurement, and reporting of assets and liabilities held by DAOs, protocol foundations, and other on-chain organisations that control funds through smart contracts and multisignature wallets.

children.name: Impairment of Unique Digital Assets
children.blurb: Impairment of unique digital assets covers non-fungible tokens, tokenized collectibles, digital art, virtual land, in-game items, and other distinct on-chain assets that are not interchangeable.

sections.body: Digital asset accounting is the practice of bringing blockchain activity into the books and records that finance teams already use. It covers reconciling on chain transfers with ledger entries, deciding what a token is worth when no active market exists, checking smart contract logic before money moves, tracking shared treasuries, and testing unique digital assets for impairment. AI is used here less as a trading oracle and more as a pattern finder, a reconciliation assistant, and a review layer over contract code and transaction histories. It can flag mismatches between wallet balances and subledgers, cluster addresses that appear to belong to the same counterparty, and summarise governance proposals from decentralised treasuries. It does not remove the need for judgement about control, ownership, and valuation inputs. The work sits at the boundary of accounting standards, cryptography, and data engineering.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The field is partly solved at the mechanical level. Basic wallet to ledger matching, transaction import, and cost basis tracking are handled by many tools, and AI can speed up exception review when volumes are high. What remains hard is valuation when markets are thin or manipulated, because a price from a decentralised exchange may not be a fair value under accounting rules. Smart contract auditing has improved with automated analysis, but formal verification is still expensive and incomplete, and economic bugs can survive a clean code review. Decentralised treasuries add governance and timing problems, since a token holder vote may change what an entity controls before the ledger reflects it. Impairment of unique digital assets is unsettled because each item may be non fungible, so comparable sales are scarce and useful lives are unclear, and the site's 222 compliance and regulation pages show how much of the surrounding work is about rules rather than arithmetic.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages under this section form a chain from raw data to judgement. Blockchain to Ledger Reconciliation is the entry point for matching on chain events to journal entries and finding breaks. Valuing Illiquid Tokens takes up the hardest measurement question, where AI can help build comparables but cannot create a market. Auditing Smart Contracts covers code review, automated testing, and the limits of what a model can prove about contract behaviour. Accounting for Decentralised Treasuries deals with shared control, proposals, and the timing of recognition when governance moves faster than the books. Impairment of Unique Digital Assets closes the set by asking when a one of a kind token has lost value and how to support that conclusion. A reader would go to the first page for reconciliation mechanics, the second for valuation methods, the third for contract risk, the fourth for treasury governance, and the fifth for impairment testing.
